remember: Fraction below half is ignored; half or more counts as a day (Rule 86 Note 2).
Non-permanent officer with three years' continuous service gets commuted leave, earned leave and LWA (Rule 86A).

questions.q: When the rate of earning leave changes, how is a fraction of half or more treated?
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 86 Note 2: half and more is reckoned as a day.

questions.q: When the rate of earning leave changes, how is a fraction below half treated?
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 86 Note 2: fraction below half is ignored.

questions.q: A non-permanent officer becomes eligible for commuted leave, earned leave and LWA after how many years of continuous service?
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 86A: three years of continuous service.

remember: Medical certificate: Civil Medical Officer not lower than Civil Surgeon (Rule 13 Note 1).
Appeal against unfitness within one month; no further appeal (Rule 13 GD 3, 7).
Late attendance: 3 days late forfeits 1 day casual leave only (Rule 14 Notes). Strike absence is Dies-Non (Rule 14A).

questions.q: Who ordinarily signs the medical certificate for appointment?
options: Civil Medical Officer not lower than a Civil Surgeon

questions.q: Within what time must a candidate declared unfit appeal?
options: One month of communication of findings
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 13 Government Decision 3.

questions.q: Is there a further appeal against the adverse finding of the Medical Officer on appeal?
options: Yes, to the Government within one month
Yes, to the Public Service Commission
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 13 Government Decision 7.

questions.q: For every three days' late attendance without permission, what is forfeited?
How is unauthorised absence for participation in a strike treated?
options: Leave without allowances counted for earned leave
Dies-Non, with no pay and allowances
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 14A: Dies-Non, not counted for earned leave.

remember: Pay is drawn from the date of assuming duties and stops when duties cease (Rule 23(a)).
Resignation is effective when accepted and officer is relieved (Rule 23 GD 1(d)).

questions.q: From when does an officer begin to draw the pay of a post?
options: From the date of the order of appointment
From the date he assumes the duties of the post
From the first of the next month

questions.q: When does a resignation become effective?
options: When accepted and the officer is relieved of duties
When the head of office receives it
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 23 Government Decision 1(d).

questions.q: When does an officer cease to draw the pay of a post?
options: At the end of the month
On the date of the relieving order
As soon as he ceases to discharge its duties

remember: Joining time on station transfer: max 30 days; 6 days preparation plus journey (Rule 127).
No change of residence: one day (Rule 126). Change of station means 8 km or more (Rule 126 Note).
Sunday not counted but included in the 30 days (Rule 127(e)). Joining time pay equals old pay; no conveyance or PTA (Rule 136).

questions.q: What is the maximum joining time on transfer from one station to another?
How many days are allowed for preparation, besides the journey time?
How much joining time is allowed when the new post involves no change of residence?
A transfer involves a change of station only if the distance is not less than how much?
Which allowances cannot be drawn during joining time?
options: House rent allowance and dearness allowance
Conveyance allowance and Permanent Travelling Allowance

remember: Sunday does not count in joining time calculation but is included in the 30-day maximum (Rule 127(e)).
Officer on joining time is on duty and gets joining time pay (Rule 136).
Transfer at own request gives no joining time (Rule 136 Note). Not joining in time: no pay (Rule 137).

questions.q: Is an officer on joining time regarded as on duty?
options: Yes, with joining time pay equal to pay drawn before relinquishing charge
Yes, with half of the pay drawn earlier
No, he gets only subsistence allowance

questions.q: When is an officer on transfer entitled to joining time?
options: Only if the transfer is made in the public interest
Only if transferred at own request
Only if station distance exceeds 20 km

questions.q: What does an officer get who does not join within joining time?
options: No pay or leave salary after the joining time ends

questions.q: How is a Sunday treated in joining time?
options: Counted as a day and included in 30 days
Counted as a day but excluded from 30 days
Not counted as a day, but included in the 30-day maximum
Neither counted nor included in 30 days

remember: Earned leave: full duty pay. Half pay/leave not due: half pay. Commuted: twice half-pay (Rules 92-94).
Leave without allowances: no leave salary (Rule 95).
HRA, CCA, Hill Tract Allowance: up to 180 days (Rule 93(iii)). Overstayal: half-pay leave if due; no leave salary if unauthorised (Rule 96).

questions.q: What is leave salary on earned leave?
options: Full duty pay with admissible allowances

questions.q: What is leave salary on commuted leave?
options: One and a half times half-pay leave salary

questions.q: What leave salary is payable on leave without allowances?
Allowances such as HRA and CCA are paid during leave for how long at a time?
options: Within 180 days, or the first 180 days of longer leave

questions.q: How is overstayal of leave treated?
options: As half-pay leave to the extent due, otherwise as leave without allowances
As earned leave to the extent due

remember: Wilful absence after expiry of leave is misbehaviour under Rule 21, Part I (Rule 96 Note).

questions.q: How is wilful absence from duty after expiry of leave treated?
options: As misbehaviour for the purpose of Rule 21, Part I

questions.q: Which rule's misbehaviour provision applies to wilful absence after leave expires?
questions.why: KSR Part I, Rule 96 Note refers to Rule 21.

questions.q: Wilful absence after leave expires is treated as what?

remember: Qualifying service: below half year ignored; half year or more rounded up (Part III Rule 57). Pension service min 10, max 30 years.
Pension in whole rupees, rounded up (Rule 58). No gratuity instead of pension (Rule 60).
Average emoluments: last ten months (Rule 63). 10 years = 10/80th; 30 years = 30/80th (Rule 64).

questions.q: How is a fraction of a year of qualifying service treated?
options: Below half year ignored; half year or more rounded up

questions.q: What are the minimum and maximum service for pension calculation?
Average emoluments are calculated on the last how many months of qualifying service?
What is pension at 30 years of qualifying service?
options: 30/80th of average emoluments, maximum Rs 7200 per annum

questions.q: Gratuity for qualifying service of 1 to 9 years is how much?
options: One month's emoluments for each completed year

remember: Government may order recovery from pension of pecuniary loss caused to it, if pensioner found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence (Part III Rule 3).

questions.q: If a pensioner is found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence, what may Government order?
options: Recovery from pension of whole or part of pecuniary loss caused to Government
Stoppage of pension for life only
Recovery of pension for the last ten months only
Reduction of pension to half in all cases

questions.q: Recovery under Rule 3 relates to which kind of loss?
The recovery under Rule 3 may be of how much of the loss?

remember: Dismissal/removal: pay ceases from that date (Rule 54).
Subsistence allowance equals half-pay leave salary on date of suspension; certificate of no other employment needed; overpayment recovery not ordinarily over one-third (Rule 55).
Suspended on LWA: none during leave; on leave with allowances: leave cancelled, gets subsistence (Rule 55B). Death during suspension: duty for all purposes (Rule 56B).

questions.q: What is the subsistence allowance of a suspended officer?
options: Leave salary on half-pay leave on the date of suspension

questions.q: What certificate is needed to draw subsistence allowance?
options: Not engaged in any other employment, business, profession or vocation

questions.q: What is the ordinary limit on recovery of overpayments from subsistence allowance?
An officer suspended while on leave with allowances: what is the effect?
options: He continues leave with full leave salary
Leave is cancelled for the suspension period and he gets subsistence allowance

questions.q: A suspended officer dies before proceedings end. How is the period from suspension to death treated?
options: As duty for all purposes, family gets full pay and allowances

remember: In other reinstatement cases, the suspension period is not duty unless the competent authority specifically directs (Rule 56B(7)).

questions.q: In other reinstatement cases, how is the suspension period treated?
options: Not as duty, unless competent authority specifically directs

questions.q: Who can direct that the suspension period be treated as duty for a specified purpose?
Under Rule 56B(7), the suspension period is treated as duty for what scope?
options: Only a specified purpose, if so directed

remember: DCRG: half of emoluments per completed year, max 15 times; max Rs 7 lakhs (Rule 68).
Death in service: min 12 times emoluments; under 5 years: 6 times, first year two months (Rule 68). Rule 67 needs 5 years.
Residuary gratuity if less than 12 times received; not if pension commuted (Rule 69).

questions.q: What is the rate of death-cum-retirement gratuity?
options: One month per year, maximum 10 times
Half of emoluments per completed year, maximum 15 times emoluments
Full emoluments per year, maximum 15 times

questions.q: What is the maximum gratuity amount under Rule 68?
What is the minimum gratuity in invalid pension or death in service?
An employee dies in service with under 5 years of service. What gratuity does the family get?
options: 6 times emoluments, but two months' emoluments if death is in first year

questions.q: Residuary gratuity applies if sums received are less than how much?

remember: Non-contributory family pension: 10 years after 20 years' service (Rule 80); half of pension, max Rs 150, min Rs 30 (Rule 82).
Not to widow with another living husband (Rule 80); one member at a time (Rule 87(a)); not for compassionate allowance families (Rule 5(aa)).
Contributory above Rs 3000: 15% of pay, min Rs 600, max Rs 1100 (Rule 90(4CC)).

questions.q: For how long is non-contributory family pension granted, after not less than 20 years' service?
What are the maximum and minimum of non-contributory family pension per month?
Who is the first claimant under Rule 85 if the deceased is a male employee?
Can non-contributory pension be paid to more than one family member at the same time?
options: Yes, to spouse and eldest son

questions.q: What is the contributory family pension for pay above Rs 3000 from 1.4.1994?
options: 15% of pay, minimum Rs 600, maximum Rs 1100
10% of pay, minimum Rs 600, maximum Rs 1100
15% of pay, minimum Rs 300, maximum Rs 1100
15% of pay, minimum Rs 600, maximum Rs 1500

remember: Maternity leave: 180 days full pay; also for temporary female officers (Rule 100).
Miscarriage: up to six weeks (Rule 101). Hysterectomy: up to 45 days (Rule 101A). Both need medical certificate.
No certificate for up to 60 days leave in continuation of maternity leave (Rule 102 Proviso).

questions.q: How many days of maternity leave on full pay can a female officer get?
What is the maximum leave for miscarriage including abortion?
What is the maximum leave for hysterectomy?
Leave up to how many days in continuation of maternity leave needs no medical certificate?
What does 'full pay' mean in the maternity leave rule?
options: Pay admissible under Rule 92, Part I, KSR

remember: Leave not due: max 360 days in entire service; 90 days at a time and 180 in all if not on medical certificate (Rule 85).
Debited against half-pay leave earned later; granted only when no other leave with allowance is available.
Cancelled if voluntary retirement is granted (Note 1); stands even if not earned later (Note 2).

questions.q: What is the maximum leave not due in the entire service?
Leave not due other than on medical certificate: what are the limits?
options: 60 days at a time and 120 days in all
90 days at a time and 180 days in all
180 days at a time and 360 days in all
30 days at a time and 90 days in all

questions.q: Against what is leave not due debited?
What happens to leave not due if voluntary retirement permission is granted?
options: It is converted to earned leave

questions.q: If an officer fails to earn the leave not due by later duty, what happens?
options: It stands, subject to his wishes
It is converted to commuted leave

remember: LWA for non-permanent officer: max 3 months on one occasion (Rule 88(ii)). Over four months: Government sanctions (Rule 64).
TB, leprosy, cancer, mental disease: leave without pay up to 18 months (Rule 90); ex-gratia 35% of basic pay (Rule 90A(a)).
Ex-gratia max: 18 months temporary, 36 months permanent (Rule 90A(e)).

questions.q: What is the LWA limit on one occasion for officers not in permanent employ?
Who sanctions leave without allowances exceeding four months at a time?
What is the maximum leave without pay for a temporary officer for TB, leprosy, cancer or mental disease?
What is the ex-gratia allowance during such leave?
options: 35 per cent of basic pay drawn just before the leave

questions.q: What is the maximum period of ex-gratia allowance for a permanent employee in entire service?

remember: Special disability leave: injury caused in official duty; must manifest within 3 months (Rule 97(1),(2)).
Max 24 months per disability; counted as duty for pension, not debited to leave account (Rule 97(5),(6)).
Leave salary: first four months as Rule 92, then Rule 93 (Rule 97(7)). Admissible to temporary officers (Rule 98 Note).

questions.q: Within what time must the disability manifest itself for special disability leave?
options: Within three months of the occurrence

questions.q: What is the maximum special disability leave for any one disability?
How is special disability leave treated for pension and the leave account?
options: Counted as duty for pension and not debited to leave account

questions.q: What is leave salary for the first four months of special disability leave?
Is disability leave admissible to temporary officers?

remember: Commutation: up to 40 per cent of pension (App X Rule 3); not during pending proceedings; application to authority sanctioning pension (Rule 4).
Restored after twelve years (Rule 6A(1)); no commuting again (Rule 6A(2)).
Reduction effective from 1st of month after commuted value is drawn (Rule 5).

questions.q: What proportion of pension can be commuted?
questions.why: KSR Part III, Appendix X, Rule 3.

questions.q: Can an officer commute pension during pendency of judicial or departmental proceedings?
questions.why: KSR Part III, Appendix X, Rule 3 proviso.

questions.q: To whom is the commutation application addressed?
questions.why: KSR Part III, Appendix X, Rule 4.

questions.q: After how many years is the commuted portion restored (retirement at age 55)?
questions.why: KSR Part III, Appendix X, Rule 6A(1).

questions.q: From when does the pension reduction take effect after commutation?
options: 1st day of the month of drawing the value
1st day of the month following the month the commuted value is drawn
questions.why: KSR Part III, Appendix X, Rule 5.

remember: Any leave may be combined with or follow any other leave, except under Appendices (Rule 73).
Eligibility decided on the date the officer proceeds on leave (Rule 73 Ruling).
Earned plus commuted leave limit 240 days; no limit on half-pay leave at a time (Rule 74); no leave beyond compulsory retirement (Rule 75).

questions.q: Can any kind of leave be combined with another kind?
options: Only casual leave can be combined

questions.q: On what date is eligibility for leave determined?
options: The date the officer proceeds on leave

questions.q: What is the limit on earned leave and commuted leave combined?
Is there a limit on half-pay leave taken at a time on medical certificate?
Can leave be granted beyond the date of compulsory retirement?
